changelog: fix: update.sh could never pull again on a machine that actually runs pipelines. backend/Rplots.pdf was committed to the repo once, long ago. It is R's default graphics device — R creates it in the working directory whenever a base-graphics call is made with no device already open — so EVERY pipeline run rewrites it, git pull aborts on the dirty tree, and update.sh stops. The more jobs a machine runs, the more certainly it is stuck; the machine whose only purpose is running jobs could never update at all. It is now swept and untracked the same way jobs_history.json already was, and gitignored, so the removal travels with this commit and the sweep keeps older clones unblocked meanwhile. Nothing reads Rplots.pdf — it is where stray plots go to be lost. Also: when update.sh does stop on genuinely modified files it now prints the stash and checkout commands with the actual paths filled in rather than a <file> placeholder, and says to check git diff --summary, because a file listed with no visible difference is a permission change rather than an edit and the two need different fixes.
